short: Face-image voice control (M07) and VAE/cross-modal training (M03) are standard: Facetron did face-derived zero-shot voice on GRID in 2021; face EER 36.72 vs 26.57 with reference audio; no WER.
position: The paper [@sheng2023zeroshot] changes two components: a face embedding instead of reference audio sets the voice at use time (M07), and training separates content from identity with a VAE prior and teaches the face encoder from a speech speaker encoder (M03). Both are standard. Facetron already predicted speaker features from face images with an encoder trained by cosine similarity to a pre-trained speech embedding, tested on held-out GRID speakers [@um2021facetron]; it is not cited, so the "first attempt" claim (Abstract) fails. The face route trails the audio route it replaces: unseen-speaker EER 36.72 against 26.57 (Table 1), 38% higher (inference). The ablations do support both training pieces. Intelligibility is unsupported: no word error is reported, though Table 2's baselines have published word error on that split [@kefalas2023large], and Table 2 scores the reference-speech model, not the zero-shot one.
